patterns.usage_note: Coordinating か lays out genuine alternatives from which one is to be settled on, which is why it fits deciding, choosing, and wondering, while や and とか merely sample a set nobody has to choose from. It attaches to nouns, plain-form verbs, i-adjectives, and た, and the final か may be dropped before a particle (お茶かコーヒーを). When the sentence is about not knowing which, the tail often becomes 〜かわからない / 〜か覚えていない. なり likewise offers options, but only as suggestions the hearer may act on; か frames alternatives whose resolution is at issue.

examples.ruby: 紅茶[こうちゃ]かコーヒーか、好[す]きな方[ほう]を選[えら]んでください。
examples.english: Tea or coffee — take whichever you prefer.

examples.ruby: 電車[でんしゃ]で来[く]るか歩[ある]いて来[く]るか、決[き]めておいて。
examples.english: Decide in advance whether you're coming by train or on foot.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]が笑[わら]ったか泣[な]いたか、よく分[わ]からなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't tell whether he was laughing or crying.
